title: RPG Maker MZ compatibility with steam features and porting

posts.author: Blackfield
posts.body:
Hi all,
My first own game went pretty well on steam with currently over 500 unit sales. Now I'm thinking about making a sequel that was in my mind already while working on Tales of Vogar.
ToV was made with MV and one of the most annoying things for me was the bad compatibility with steam (lots of adjustments and plugins needed, steam achievements was a pain ... ) and that there was pretty much no way to port to consoles. Is this any different with MZ? These two things were the ones that annoyed me the most - after all, steam and porting to consoles are the best ways to bring the game to the people.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
They're basically the same.
The only real difference is that MZ starts with a higher version of NW.js - I don't know if you had to interact with that at all for your Steam stuff with the MV project.
But it would theoretically provide access to some more modern JavaScript functions if that helps you with the Steam API.
Aside from that, they have for the majority part the same codebase, and they're both based on HTML - so if that gave you a problem with porting to consoles, MZ is exactly the same.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body: There's RPG Maker Unite, which is a Unity mod so should be as portable as that is; but as far as I've heard, it's pretty much a hot turd as far as a piece of software goes.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Blackfield said:
Is there any plan in the future for a new RPG Maker that will have better porting?
Click to expand...
Unfortunately, I don't think any of us here have any more information on if or when the next RM will appear, and what features it might have.
As Turan said, Unite...exists, but it probably shouldn't.
It's probably far more complicated than it's worth, but I believe I have heard that RM games that have been ported to consoles are basically in a C#/C++ wrapper, and typically that is handled by another game engine, such as Unity or Unreal.
This is all conjecture, so take it with a grain of salt.
I suggest looking into finding a publisher who also publishes on consoles. Depending on their contract they may require publishing on consoles, but as a result, may also assist with such a task. I'd look for publishers who have published RM games on consoles, as they probably already have the technical know how.
Edit:
On an completely unrelated note, you should look at the thing in my signature about MV crashing - judging by this review left on your game.

Watch the double posting.
No, you can't remove steam reviews, otherwise all the shady devs out there with their shovelware games would probably remove all the negative reviews to make their game look like it's showered with praise.
I also wouldn't take it personally. People tend to hone in on negative aspects more than positive aspects. If something breaks in a game people are far more likely to leave a negative review.
Anyways, glad you got it fixed.
No game engine is going to make everything easy, otherwise we'd all be putting our dream game out there without breaking a sweat. RPG Maker makes a lot of things easy, but there's still a lot of work involved, as you know, and part of that is integrating APIs and porting.
If you're between games, it might be a good time to take a moment to check out other engines, play around with them, and see if they are something you can get comfortable with. The big 3, Unity, Unreal, and Godot all have support for console porting (well, I am not 100% sure about Godot, but I am like...90% sure). There are also other RPG Maker-like engines out there you could look into. They are considered competition with RM, and considering this is the official RM site we're technically not suppose to talk about them. But a quick google search for "RPG Maker competitor" or similar terminology will turn up some results.
Good luck with your next game!
